key_insight: MACE-driven molecular dynamics can rapidly reproduce DFT sorption trends for point defects in 2D materials and extend the screening to finite temperature.
engineering_relevance: This enables much faster prescreening of defect candidates for sorption-related applications in 2D materials, reducing reliance on expensive first-principles workflows.
method: Simulated 17,624 defect structures from the ADAQ database with MACE-accelerated molecular dynamics.
Compared sorption behavior at 0 K against prior high-throughput DFT results.
Extended the analysis to 300 K to assess finite-temperature robustness.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that MACE reproduces the overall DFT sorption trends at 0 K and that the qualitative trends remain largely unchanged at 300 K.
watch_item: MACE is suitable for prescreening, but DFT is still needed for accurate quantitative validation of promising defect candidates.
paper_title: Sorption Molecular Dynamics of Point Defects in 2D Materials with a Machine Learning Potential
